title: Introduce prefill orchestrator + warmup prober and tenant quant cohortizer (traffic sandbox)
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a heuristic prefill orchestrator and non-disruptive warmup prober plus a tenant quantization cohortizer. Backwards compatible; feature gated behind `prefill.experimental` and `quant.cohorts` toggles. Includes CLI dry-run and telemetry.
description: This PR adds a lightweight prefill orchestrator that synthesizes tenant signals (recent latency, token distribution, burstiness) to produce safe defaults for batching, cache TTLs, and quantization cohort recommendations. It also introduces a warmup prober that runs mirrored, low-impact sampling against a safe sandbox to warm KV caches and validate candidate batch shapes without affecting production capacity. The third major piece is a quant cohortizer which assigns tenants to one of several quant cohorts (fp16, int8, q4, q4_0) using a conservative gating policy and staged rollout plan with automatic rollback hooks. Motivation: many tenants run with conservative defaults and manual tuning is costly; automating safe initial defaults reduces tail latency/cost for most customers while preserving manual overrides and safe fallbacks. This change is intentionally conservative: everything is disabled by default and requires the `prefill.experimental=true` flag or a tenant opt-in. Key features: CLI dry-run mode (`rwd prefill plan --dry-run`) that simulates assignment and outputs unit-econ delta, a traffic-sandbox mode that mirrors 0.1% of traffic for validation, per-tenant rollback hooks, telemetry for cohort delta (latency/cost/accuracy heuristics), unit tests and integration smoke harness. Deployment notes: enable feature flags in helm (values.prefill.experimental) to opt-in; run the included dry-run against representative traffic before enabling. Checklist: 1) implement orchestrator core and cohortizer policy, 2) add warmup prober with safe mirroring, 3) CLI dry-run and plan exporter, 4) telemetry metrics and dashboards, 5) integration tests and canary rollout plan. Related: ENG-4312 (prefill policy spec), ENG-5421 (warmup sampling pilot).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This is promising. Concern: how do we ensure mirrored traffic can't exhaust experimental capacity? Suggest hard cap and backpressure path.
Ava Martinez: Added a global mirror cap and per-tenant throttles in mirror.go; default mirror rate 0.1% and a tunable max-requests-sampled flag. Updated docs with cap behaviour.
Priya Desai: Need stronger safety gating around quant cohort assignment — prefer a staged rollout with cohort A/B and immediate kickback to fp16 on error spikes.
Ava Martinez: Implemented staged rollout state machine and immediate fallback to fp16 if latency or error rate exceeds thresholds (configurable). Added unit tests for rollback path.
Jorge Alvarez: Can we calculate unit-econ delta in the dry-run output? That will help product and SRE make decisions.
Ava Martinez: Dry-run now outputs estimated token-cost delta and expected latency impact per tenant, plus a CSV for offline analysis.
Liam O'Connor: CI failed once due to flaky integration test; re-run looked good. Approving pending small nits in docs.
Priya Desai: Approved — nice safety-first approach.
